nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal whose variable $x$ occurs in $F$. Then the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$ has strictly fewer distinct variables than $F$.
nodes.title: Restriction reduces the number of variables

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal $(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF $\mathcal{A}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the disjoining builder $\mathcal{O}_p$. For an atom $a$, $\mathcal{A}_p(a, S)$ is the unit clause…
nodes.title: Accumulating CNF builder

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For a polarity $p$ and a proposition $\varphi$, the CNF of $\varphi$ at polarity $p$ is the result of the accumulating CNF builder at polarity $p$ on $\varphi$ with the empty CNF as accumulator; the atom $a$ becomes the variable $\iota(a)$.
nodes.title: CNF of a proposition at a polarity

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal $(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF $\mathcal{O}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the accumulating CNF builder $\mathcal{A}_p$. Write $X \otimes S$ for the disjunction of two CNFs $X$ and…
nodes.title: Disjoining CNF builder

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfiability means having a satisfying assignment

nodes.summary: Let the atoms have a distinguished atom $\bot$ and let $\iota$ be an injective numbering of the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$, the CNF consisting of the unit clause with the single negative literal on variable $\iota(\bot)$ followed by the clauses of the CNF of $A$ (atom $a$ read as variable $\iota(a)$) is satisfiable if and only if some valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false makes…
nodes.title: Satisfiability of a CNF with falsum false

nodes.summary: A CNF formula is a finite list of CNF clauses, read as the conjunction of its clauses.
nodes.title: CNF formula

nodes.summary: A CNF clause is a finite list of literals, each a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$.
nodes.title: CNF clause

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable when there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that every clause $C$ of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Satisfiability of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: For CNFs $\varphi = C_1 \land \dots \land C_m$ and $\psi = D_1 \land \dots \land D_n$, their disjunction is the CNF with one clause $C_i \lor D_j$ (the literals of $C_i$ followed by those of $D_j$) for each pair $(i, j)$, listed with $i$ as the outer and $j$ as the inner index. It expresses $(\bigwedge_i C_i) \lor (\bigwedge_j D_j)$ as $\bigwedge_{i,j} (C_i \lor D_j)$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of two CNFs

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $F$ and every literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the variable $x$ does not occur in the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$.
nodes.title: The restricted variable no longer occurs

nodes.summary: Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction of a CNF formula $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is obtained by deleting every clause of $\varphi$ that contains $\ell$ and replacing every other clause by its restriction by $\ell$, the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity; the remaining clauses keep their order.
nodes.title: Restriction of a CNF formula by a literal

nodes.summary: Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction of a clause by $\ell$ is the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity, keeping the other literals in order.
nodes.title: Restriction of a clause by a literal

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula that contains the unit clause whose only literal is $\ell$. Then $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Unit propagation preserves satisfiability

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $F$ and every variable $x$, the formula $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is satisfiable or the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Splitting on a variable

nodes.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF clause $C$ when at least one literal of $C$ is satisfied by $v$, that is, $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a clause

nodes.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF formula $\varphi$ when $v$ satisfies every clause of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $v_1, v_2$ be assignments of Booleans to variables with $v_1(x) = v_2(x)$ for every variable $x$ occurring in $F$. If $v_1$ satisfies $F$, then $v_2$ satisfies $F$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables. If $v$ satisfies the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$, then the assignment that agrees with $v$ except that it sends $x$ to $b$ satisfies $F$.
nodes.title: Lifting a satisfying assignment from a restriction

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a restricted CNF formula

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a clause, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal that does not occur in $C$, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the restriction of $C$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $C$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a restricted clause

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$ and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables, the CNF of $A$ built with atom $a$ as variable $\iota(a)$ is satisfied by $\sigma$ if and only if $A$ evaluates to true under the valuation $\sigma \circ \iota$ of the atoms.
nodes.title: Equivalent CNF

nodes.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a literal $(x, b)$, with variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, when $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a literal

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity true, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.
nodes.title: CNF of a proposition

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The complement CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity false, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.
nodes.title: CNF of the complement of a proposition

nodes.summary: The variables of a CNF formula $\varphi$ form the union of the sets of variables of its clauses, that is, the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.
nodes.title: Variables of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $(x, b)$ a literal. If $x$ is a variable of $\varphi$, then the set of variables of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $(x, b)$ is a proper subset of the set of variables of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Restricting by an occurring variable shrinks the variable set

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ and every literal $\ell$, every variable of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is a variable of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Restriction does not add variables

nodes.summary: The variables of a CNF clause $C$ form the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.
nodes.title: Variables of a clause

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
